repository.name: @webex/plugin-encryption
repository.purpose: Public Webex JS SDK plugin registered as webex.cypher that downloads and decrypts encrypted Webex files. downloadAndDecryptFile reads the KMS key URI and the JWE-encrypted SCR from the keyUri and JWE query parameters of the file URL, or from the options, asks webex.internal.encryption to decrypt the SCR with the KMS key, and returns the internal download of the file decrypted with that SCR, either directly from the URL (the default) or through the Webex files service. register and deregister register the SDK device with WDM through webex.internal.device and track the result in a registered flag. The package main, src/webex.js, is a small CommonJS Webex constructor that loads only the authorization, internal encryption, and cypher plugins; the workspace also builds it as the UMD encryption bundle.

public_interfaces.name: @webex/plugin-encryption package main
public_interfaces.audience: applications that only download and decrypt files
public_interfaces.notes: main and exports['.'] load dist/webex.js, whose CommonJS export is a Webex constructor with authorization, internal encryption, and cypher. Webex.init merges the compiled webex-config module object, so its defaults land under config.default and are not applied, and the types entry declares a default Cypher instead; both are known defects in the module spec Evidence register.

public_interfaces.name: cypher plugin registration and types
public_interfaces.audience: SDK bundles (webex, webex-node) and TypeScript consumers
public_interfaces.notes: Registers public plugin cypher with config {cypher: {}}; first registration of the name wins. Requiring the package loads the main, which requires this entry, so the webex and webex-node packages get cypher as a side effect. devMain and the typedoc entry point here, but no workspace resolver reads devMain; types is dist/types/index.d.ts, emitted by yarn build.

public_interfaces.name: webex.cypher methods
public_interfaces.notes: register and deregister call webex.internal.device and flip the registered flag only on success; registered is a public writable field, so callers can also set it without a device call. downloadAndDecryptFile takes keyUri and JWE from the URL query, else both from options.keyUri and options.jwe, calls internal decryptScr then download with useFileService (default false). decryptScr errors are wrapped with cause (MOD-008); download errors are not (a known defect).

public_interfaces.name: package scripts
public_interfaces.notes: build:src compiles src to dist with webex-legacy-tools and then runs build, which emits declarations to dist/types. test:unit runs jest with an 85% global coverage threshold (jest.config.js). test:browser runs nothing because there is no test/integration directory. build:docs writes typedoc output outside the package. There is no aggregate test script and no test:integration script.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not decrypt, fetch keys, or download in this plugin; call webex.internal.encryption.
negative_guidance.why: One implementation of key handling and download rules (module spec Design overview).

negative_guidance.rule: Do not mix a key URI from the URL with a JWE from the options.
negative_guidance.why: They are one pair from one source (INV-001).

negative_guidance.rule: Do not log key URIs, JWEs, SCRs, file bytes, or tokens.
negative_guidance.why: They grant access to encrypted content (INV-003).

negative_guidance.rule: Do not assume src/webex-config.ts defaults apply to Webex.init instances.
negative_guidance.why: They are merged under config.default (a known defect in the module spec Evidence register).

negative_guidance.rule: Do not trust a test:unit result without a fresh build:src of the sibling packages.
negative_guidance.why: The unit spec imports @webex/internal-plugin-encryption by name, which loads its dist.

high.expectation: Source and a unit case agree, as for register, deregister, the options fallback, and the missing-values rejection.

medium.expectation: Only source or a generator probe exists, as for the URL-wins rule, Webex.init, and the known defects. Pin current behavior with a unit case before modifying.

low.expectation: Neither source, tests, nor a dependency's spec or code settles the question, as for why the invalid-URL message names the JWE. Stop and report the gap.
